title: राणाकालीन जिल्ला प्रशासनमा बडाहाकिम व्यवस्था {Badahakim (the Chief Magistrate) in District Administration during Rana Resigme}
authors: के  सी KC, तेज बहादर Tej Bahadur
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख राणाकलीन जिल्ला प्रशासन अन्तरगत सम्पूर्ण जिल्लाको जिम्मेवारी दिने गरी श्री ३ बाट आफनो प्रतिनिधिको रुपमा नियुक्त गरिने बडाहाकिमसँग सम्बन्धित छ । जसरी केन्द्र र प्रान्तमा श्री ३ ले आफना अधिकारको प्रयोग गरी राज्यसञ्ंचालन गर्ने गर्दथे, त्यसरी नै जिल्लामा श्री ३ को उत्तराधिकारीको रुपमा सम्पूर्ण अधिकारको प्रयोग गरि जिल्ला संञ्चालन गर्ने प्रमुख प्रशासकीय पद थियो वडाहाकिम । बडाहाकिमको नियुक्ति सिधै श्री ३ बाट हुने गर्दथ्यो। खासगरी राणा परिवारका सदस्य र उनीहरुको परीवारसँग सम्बन्धित विश्वास पात्र ब्यक्तिहरुबाट वडाहाकिमको नियुक्ति गरिन्थ्यो । कहिलेकाही श्री ३ को रोलक्रममा रहेको ब्यक्तिलाई श्री ३ ले उपत्यकाबाट बाहिर राख्नुपर्ने आबस्यकता महसुस गरेमा त्यस्ता ब्यक्तिहरुलाई पनि वडाहाकिम नियुक्त गरी पठाएका पाइन्छ। वडाहाकिम गौडा र छाटीगाडाको प्रमुख प्रशासकिय पद हो । जिल्लाभित्रका सम्पूर्णकार्यालयहरुको अनुगमन , रेखदेख, नियन्त्रण, र निर्देशन गर्नु,जिल्लामा शान्ति सुरक्षा कायम राख्नु , जनतामा अन्याय अत्याचार हुन नदिनु , राणा विरोधी गतिविधि माथि रोक लगाउनु, कर्मचारीको निष्पक्ष मूल्याङकन गरी पजनीका लागि श्री ३ लाई विवरण पठाइ सहयोग गर्नु, छिमेकी देश खासगरी भारतसँगको सम्बन्धमा मित्रता कायम गर्नु, राजश्व संकलन गरी देशको ढुकुटी मजबुत बनाउनु र आफनो कायको मूल्याङकन गर्न केन्द्र बाट आउने गुप्तचर र दौडाहलाई नकारात्मक विवरण लेखी श्री ३ मा पेसगर्ने मौका नदिनु वडाहाकिमका मुख्य कार्य थिए । {                 Abstract Thee presented article is related to the Chief Magistrate who will be appointed as hisrepresentative from His Highness Sir Shree 3 used to run the state using his powers in the centerand the province, in the district as the successor of His Highness, the chief administrativeposition was to run the district using all the powers. american_english: The present article relates to the Badahakim, who was appointed as a representative by the Shree 3 with full responsibility for an entire district under district administration during the Rana period. Just as the Shree 3 exercised his powers to govern the state at the center and in the provinces, in the districts the Badahakim was the chief administrative position that governed the district by exercising full authority as the Shree 3's successor. The appointment of the Badahakim was made directly by the Shree 3. In particular, the Badahakim was appointed from members of the Rana family and trustworthy persons related to their family. Occasionally, if the Shree 3 felt the need to keep an individual in the roll order outside the Valley, such individuals were also appointed as Badahakim and dispatched. The Badahakim was the chief administrative position of a gauda and chhotigauda. The primary duties of the Badahakim were to monitor, supervise, control, and direct all offices within the district; maintain peace and security in the district; prevent injustice and oppression against the people; curb anti-Rana activities; assist the Shree 3 by impartially evaluating employees and submitting reports for pajani; maintain friendly relations with neighboring countries, especially India; strengthen the national treasury by collecting revenue; and give no opportunity for spies and inspection tours (daudaha) coming from the center to evaluate his work to submit negative reports to the Shree 3.
